model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared only the available official measurements and noted that the prior tile results confound CTA size with staged payload; this candidate still requires controller validation and timing.

memory_lessons.applicability: Same CUDA n-body kernel and official measurement context; the comparison motivates a configuration that changes source payload while retaining the 256-thread tile.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 128-thread compact-tile candidate was faster than the measured 256-thread full-Particle-tile candidate, and both were correct. Because both tile size and staged payload differed, those results do not establish which change explains the timing difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a 256-thread compact-source tile under the same official protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: Keeping a 256-thread CTA and 256-source tile while staging only x, y, z, and mass reduces dynamic shared-memory use from the previously measured full-Particle tile configuration without reducing source reuse per CTA. The measurements for the earlier 128-thread compact tile and 256-thread full-Particle tile do not isolate those factors; this candidate tests a 256-thread compact tile.

retained: Keep a 256-thread CTA with a matching 256-source tile, and set the dynamic shared-memory allocation to 4096 bytes for four floats per source.
Cooperatively stage only source x, y, z, and mass; synchronize before tile consumption and before shared-memory reuse.
Preserve one target and force accumulator per active thread, bound the final partial tile, skip self-interactions using global source indices, and write every valid target exactly once.
